findings.title: Federated recovery-code creation drops credential metadata
findings.body: When a user-storage provider accepts the update, it receives only an empty credential ID, the type, and a JSON array of raw codes. The supplied RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel, which carries the verified generated-at timestamp and user label, is otherwise discarded. Unlike the local fallback, a storage provider therefore cannot reconstruct the same credential metadata; recovery-code labels and the original creation time are lost for federated users and will be missing or incorrect in credential/account representations. Pass the required metadata in the storage update contract (for example, a recovery-code-specific input/serialized DTO) rather than only the code list.

findings.title: Exhausted federated recovery credentials are removed through the local-store API
findings.body: getCredential() now returns a credential from user storage before consulting local storage, but this branch still calls removeStoredCredentialById(), which operates on the stored/local credential path. An exhausted credential returned by a user-storage provider is therefore not removed by this call. Providers that retain a credential with all codes marked used can remain configured with an unusable recovery credential, leaving stale data and potentially causing subsequent recovery flows to request a non-existent next code. Deletion needs to be dispatched to the credential's actual source, or federated providers need an explicit, enforced exhausted-credential lifecycle.

findings.title: The new user-storage fixture accepts the same recovery code indefinitely
findings.body: The recovery-code validator only checks whether the submitted raw code is present in the persisted list and never removes it or records it as used. getCredentials() consequently reconstructs every code as unused on every request. The added integration test validates one successful login only, so it would pass even though a recovery code can be replayed without limit. Persist consumed-code state (or remove the code) in the fixture and add a second-login assertion that reuse is rejected.
